'''Dr Mervyn Charles Probine''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|CB|FRSNZ|size=85%}} (30 April 1924 – 17 April 2010) was a New Zealand physicist and public servant. He served as chairman of the [[State Services Commission]] between 1981 and 1986.

==Early life and family==
Born in [[Auckland]] on 30 April 1924, Probine was the son of Frederick Charles Probine and Annie Kathleen Probine (née Polson).<ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/NZH19240503.2.2.2 |title=Births |date=3 May 1924 |page=1 |work=New Zealand Herald |accessdate=23 July 2020}}</ref> He married Marjorie Walker in 1949, and the couple went on to have two children.<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_3597666"/>

==Career==
Probine joined the [[Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (New Zealand)|Department of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (DSIR) as a draughtsman in 1942.<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_3597666">{{cite news |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/3597666/Former-State-Services-Commission-boss-dies |title=Former State Services Commission boss dies |date=19 April 2010 |agency=[[NZPA]] |work=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |accessdate=23 October 2011}}</ref> He graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] from [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]] in 1947 and a [[Master of Science]] from 1951 from [[Victoria University of Wellington|Victoria University College]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university19.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: P |website=Shadows of Time |accessdate=23 July 2020}}</ref> and obtained a [[PhD]] in physics from the [[University of Leeds]].<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_3597666"/> In 1967, he was appointed director of the Physics and Engineering Laboratory (PEL), and then ten years later, was promoted to assistant director-general of the DSIR.<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_3597666"/>

Dr Probine joined the [[State Services Commission]] in 1979,<ref name="henderson">
{{cite book|author=Henderson, Alan|title=The Quest for Efficiency:The Origins of the State Services Commission|year=1990 |publisher=State Services Commission |isbn=0-477-05538-9}}
</ref> and was appointed chair of that body in 1981.<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_3597666"/> During his tenure, the [[Official Information Act 1982]] was passed and the Equal Employment Opportunities Unit (EEOU) was established.<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_3597666"/> The EEOU was charged with promoting and monitoring access to employment opportunities in the New Zealand public service for ethnic minorities, women, and the disabled.<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_3597666"/>

==Honours and awards==
In 1964, Dr Probine was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/p-r/ |title=List of all Fellows with surnames P–R |publisher=Royal Society Te Apārangi |accessdate=23 July 2020}}</ref> In the [[1986 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|1986 New Year Honours]], he was appointed a [[Companion of the Order of the Bath]], in recognition of his service as chairman of the State Services Commission.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=50362 |date=31 December 1985 |page=29 |supp=2}}</ref>

==Death==
Dr Probine died in Auckland on 17 April 2010.<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_3597666"/> His wife, Marjorie, died in 2023.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.legacy.com/nz/obituaries/nzherald-nz/name/marjorie-probine-obituary?id=52658531 |title=Marjorie Probine obituary |date=10 August 2023 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=10 August 2023}}</ref>
